incidents-bot: P1 ALERT — decode-stream cluster (us-west-2) reporting repeated GPU OOMs + container restarts on nodes gpu-decode-1..4. Paging ops-oncall (Sam). Automatic token-shedding triggered.

ops-oncall (Sam): oncall here, pulling logs and metrics now. any quick hits? :eyes: 

maria.engineering: initial look — several long-running streaming requests with huge `max_tokens` and malformed client loops. looks like a token-spiral from a bot client that never closed the stream. saw repeated allocation spikes right before OOM.

julia-ml: logs show `CUDA out of memory` at decode step each time. snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T15:12:03Z] ERROR decode_worker: cudaMemcpy failed: out of memory
[2026-03-17T15:12:03Z] ERROR stream_session: generation aborted, kv_cache size spike 7.8GB -> 11.4GB
[2026-03-17T15:12:03Z] containerd: restarting container decode-srv (exit code 137)
```

leo-support: CS report: several customers saw streaming timeouts and partial outputs — top affected is AcmeChat (tenant: acct-3245). They reported ~30% request failures between 15:10-15:40.

maria.engineering: interestingly affected requests had `client_max_tokens` header missing and we defaulted to an unconstrained path. router didn't enforce `hard_token_cap`. looks like a config drift after the last rollout.

ops-oncall (Sam): immediate mitigations I'm applying now — 1) enable temporary hard cap at router (max_tokens=1024) 2) add token-based rate-limiting per-tenant 3) quarantine tenant acct-3245 while we investigate (drop new streams).

incidents-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED — router:apply-hard-cap, quota:tenant-quarantine, nodes:mark-drain (gpu-decode-1..4).

julia-ml: also enabling fallback routing to smaller quantized variant (gptq-*-small) for streaming endpoints to reduce per-request GPU memory. will prefer CPU fallback for any suspicious client.

ops-oncall (Sam): draining gpu-decode-2 and restarting process to clear leaks. applied `kubectl drain node/gpu-decode-2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then `kubectl rollout restart ds/decode-srv -n inference`.

maria.engineering: telemetry — memory 95th percentile spiked to >94% before OOM. request-drop rate peaked to 43% on streaming shard us-west-2/stream-03. KV cache growth correlated to very long prefix lengths.

leo-support: I've sent initial CS note to AcmeChat saying we mitigated and are quarantining the noisy tenant, working on root cause, will follow up with detailed postmortem.

ops-oncall (Sam): after restart and hard cap, new OOM occurrences dropped to zero in last 6 minutes. nodes stable: gpu-decode-1..4 showing normal memory patterns now. keeping drains in place while we monitor.

julia-ml: root cause hypothesis: client-side runaway generation (no max_tokens) + router config rollback removed the enforcement rule. that allowed unbounded KV cache growth producing OOMs during decode streaming.

maria.engineering: planned next steps: 1) revert the rollout that removed `hard_token_cap` guard 2) add unit/e2e test to assert router enforces `max_tokens` for streaming 3) add telemetry alert on KV cache growth per request 4) create a tenant-quarantine playbook.

ops-oncall (Sam): handoff to night oncall @kara-platform in 30m. leaving short summary:
- incident: GPU OOMs causing container restarts and request drops
- impact: streaming request failures, AcmeChat impacted (~30% errors window)
- mitigations applied: router hard cap (1024), tenant quarantine acct-3245, node restarts, fallback routing to quantized smaller variants
- status: nodes stable, drop rate returned to baseline, monitoring on for 2h

kara-platform: taking oncall. thanks Sam — I'll watch for regressions and coordinate postmortem. please paste the rollout id to revert and any PR numbers.

maria.engineering: revert PR is #4521, rollout id r-2026-03-17-17. also filing a postmortem ticket PMT-8972 and adding AcmeChat as P0 customer for comms.

leo-support: will schedule a 1:1 with AcmeChat + send interim incident summary.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigations successful, status: monitoring. oncall_handoff sam -> kara-platform.

kara-platform: acknowledged. logging this thread into incident tracker and will run the quarantine playbook tomorrow morning for follow-up. :white_check_mark:

maria.engineering: note for postmortem: consider adding router-side synthetic `max_tokens` enforcement as a permanent safety net, and an automated tenant throttling rule for abnormal token/time ratios.

ops-oncall (Sam): closing active paging. will remain available for questions. good work team. :thumbsup:
